master.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a PORTRAIT mobile puzzle-game ENVIRONMENT BACKGROUND for Starfall's Lantern Landing at 100% restored. Intended canvas 1024 x 2048 (tall 1:2 portrait). BACKGROUND ONLY: the real game will place its own crystal star pieces and controls above this painting.

REFERENCES:
Image 1: previous Lantern Landing close-up. Use its rosewood dock, rounded rope posts, hinged cream-and-brass lantern and lavender cloud materials ONLY. Its composition is WRONG: completely redesign camera and placement. Remove all six decorative characters.
Image 2: actual Starfall phone gameplay screenshot. Use its quiet centered square play area, floating foreground stars and uncluttered hierarchy as a COMPOSITION constraint only. Do not include that screenshot's moon, boat, any text, characters, streaks or UI.

PRIMARY CORRECTION:
We are now floating HIGH ABOVE Lantern Landing, looking DOWN at the place from a gently angled bird's-eye / 70-degree overhead camera. The camera has pulled back substantially. This must read as a PLAYABLE GAME ZONE with dimensional scenic corners, not a cinematic landscape, a horizon view, a close-up dock, a dollhouse portrait, or a rectangular painting behind a UI card. Think physical board-game environment discipline: broad calm center, charming tangible surroundings that belong to one location.

COMPOSITION, STRICT:
The central gameplay region occupies x=3% to 97% of image width and y=28% to 73% of image height. This entire large square-like region must be an uninterrupted, very dark midnight-indigo pocket of open sky, with only extremely faint atmospheric depth. Absolutely NO structures, ropes, posts, bright stars, plank seams, clouds, dramatic nebula, decorative frame, glowing border, grid, bright rays or reflections inside that reserved area. No visible rectangle delimiting the zone. It is open sky in the world, not a panel.
The location's main little wooden dock and its warm generous lantern are seen from ABOVE at the upper-left/upper-middle, wholly above y=25%. Their scale is smaller than the earlier close-up but the lantern remains a readable distinct landmark. Top-down roof/panel faces and plank surfaces are visible, no front-facing scenic horizon. Build one lovely small cluster: rounded rosewood arrival deck, rope posts, a bench, one big cream-and-brass lantern on a short sturdy mast, lavender pennants. The upper ceramic lantern shutters are OPEN and amber light warms ONLY that dock cluster.
At upper right, a narrow curved gangway leads off the dock toward a cloud bank at the outer edge. Its rails stay above y=25% or at the far outer edges, NEVER through the playable sky.
At the bottom below y=78%, a near curved edge of another part of the same landing, a mooring post, coiled rope and soft lavender cloud fringe give the composition foreground depth. Keep central bottom x=25..75% mostly dark and uncluttered for small native controls. No big message plaque. Use asymmetry, connected craftsmanship and three dimensional contact shadows.
A few cloud banks occupy upper and lower outer corners, with a soft atmospheric gap separating them from the large playable center. The sky connects naturally through the whole composition. No visible horizon, no row of distant mountains or islands behind a close-up stage.
The scene remains midnight even when fully restored. Warmth stays in the lantern's corner, not under gameplay pieces.

STYLE:
Premium stylized 3D storybook puzzle-game artwork, broad readable forms, thick rounded rosewood planks, aged golden brass, cream ceramic, soft lavender cloud volume. Softly painted materials with simplified detail at phone scale. The center must stay visually subordinate to the colorful star pieces that will later be rendered over it. No characters or eyes anywhere. No text, no title, no letters, no UI, no watermark, no game pieces, no visible cells.
